newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala rebels turn in all their arms - U.N..
newsitem.headline: Guatemala rebels turn in all their arms - U.N..

text.p: Guatemalan guerrillas have turned in all their weapons and were unlikely to rearm and renew their 36-year rebellion against the state, a United Nations official said on Wednesday.

"We have no reason to doubt because they have shown complete will to comply with peace accords," Lt. Col. Alfredo Crespo, spokesman for the United Nations military observer mission that verified guerrilla disarmament, told reporters.

Former combatants of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG), an umbrella group of rebel factions, lived in disarmament camps in April and May where they turned in weapons under terms of a Dec. 29 peace treaty.
Crespo said he was not authorised to release figures on how many weapons the guerrillas had turned over, but he said a much-publicised number of 1,800 "is pretty close."
An official total will come out in a final report by Spanish Gen. Jose Rodriguez, the chief of the United Nations military observers, Crespo said.
Some army officials and right-wing members of the Guatemalan Congress have challenged the credibility of the URNG, claiming the rebels were holding back weapons.
"That is speculation that has absolutely nothing to do with reality," Crespo said.
Elsewhere in Central America, peace accords ending civil wars were being endangered by groups of rearmed rebels, but Crespo said those problems were not anticipated in Guatemala.
He said the URNG did not have as many sophisticated weapons as rebel movements in El Salvador or Nicaragua. "The guerrillas here had scarce support...the guerrillas here were poor," Crespo said.

According to Crespo, claims that the URNG had hidden weapons were based on a misunderstanding of the numbers. He said 2,928 URNG members demobilized in the camps, which made people believe there should be more weapons.

But only 800 to 1,100 members were active combatants who turned over a variety of weapons including Second World War-vintage carbines to AK-47 submachine guns, he said. The rest of the guerrillas belonged to reserve forces or members of urban fronts and did not carry weapons.
The URNG, the government and the United Nations have agreed that the military observers will turn over all the weapons to the government on or about May 17, Crespo said.
